title: Southern Qi
capsule: The Southern Qi (南齊, 479–502) was the second of the Southern Dynasties of China, established when the general Xiao Daocheng deposed the last Liu Song emperor and proclaimed himself Emperor Gao in 479. The dynasty was marked by intense factional violence at court, with Emperor Ming (r. 494–498) conducting a series of purges that decimated the imperial clan, and it produced only seven emperors in twenty-three years. It was overthrown from within when the general Xiao Yan, a member of the Xiao clan, deposed the last emperor and founded the Liang dynasty in 502; in its brief existence Southern Qi held the Yangtze basin and maintained sporadic conflict with the Northern Wei across the Huai River frontier.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory in the Yangtze basin is attested through the official history (Nan Qi Shu); the northern frontier with the Northern Wei was contested and fluctuated with campaigns, making precise boundaries approximate.
